messages.subject: NoviceQues.,Part2
parts:
Thanks to all who replied to my message. I appreciate the input. Some
additional points I should have mentioned:
1. I realize that density near the road may not reflect overall density.
The point of this study is to determine the most practical, not necessarily
most accurate, method. We know there is the way things should be done and
the way they are done.
2. In this case, 97% of the forest is in 1 forest type (different
silvicultural treatments throughout, will be sampled in proportion to
availability).
3. I'll be comparing the results of spotlighting to pellet group counts and
automatic camera estimates (both conducted throughout the forest), so I
should see how near-road vs. interior densities relate. This may allow for
use of spotlight data as a covariate predictor.
4. There will be >100 marked deer present, so mark-resight data gathered
during distance sampling will also show how road vs. interior densities
compare.
Any other thoughts?
Thanks Again,
CL
